title: Antennas
blurb: The big idea before the cards.

lines.caption: An antenna turns the power from your radio into radio waves. Its length is chosen to fit the wave.
lines.label: cut to fit the wave

lines.caption: A shorter antenna fits a shorter wave, so it is resonant at a higher frequency.
lines.label: shorter: higher frequency

lines.caption: On the 2 meter band, a quarter of a wave is about 19 inches. That is the size of a common vertical antenna.
lines.label: 19 inches on 2 meters

lines.caption: Antennas do not send your signal equally everywhere. A dipole is strongest broadside, at right angles to its wire.
lines.label: strongest broadside

lines.caption: A beam antenna, such as a Yagi, concentrates the signal in one direction. That extra strength is called gain.
lines.label: a beam has gain
